newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOE would prefer rates 0.25 point higher - Davies.
newsitem.headline: BOE would prefer rates 0.25 point higher - Davies.

text.p: The Bank of England (BOE) would prefer to see interest rates a quarter of one percent higher than at present, Howard Davies, deputy governor of the Bank of England, told reporters on Wednesday.
Referring to the BOE's latest publication of its opinion on interest rates, he said: "We would have preferred to see interest rates at one quarter of one percent higher than they are."
Davies said that at the moment, differences in views on interest rates between British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and the Bank of England were not great.
After a speech to the Federation of Bankers' Associations of Japan in Tokyo, Davies was asked in a question and answer session about the BOE's independence.
He said the BOE is now allowed to publish its own views and markets can see the difference in views between the BOE and the chancellor of the exchequer.
He then referred to interest rates as an example of such a difference in view.
Japan's Jiji news agency reported Davis as saying that sterling was slightly too high against the mark.
However, Davies later said that his reported remarks about the pound/mark rate reflected the view of financial markets and not the BOE, a British embassy spokesman in Tokyo told Reuters.

"Looking at the forward rate for the pound, it seems that the market is indicating that the pound's future value would level out or drop against the mark," the embassy spokesman quoted Davies as saying.
Davies is in Tokyo on a four-day official visit. He leaves for Britain on Thursday.
